endorsements.quote: As such, it is essential to have a governing body in place to effectively guide the deployment of technologies such as AI to manage the scale and speed of transformation that will take place in healthcare organizations.
A governance framework should outline a clear accountability structure.

Embedding these types of assessment mechanisms in the governance process allows for a more thorough understanding of the AI system being implemented, and most importantly, one that is aligned with the organizations values.

unlisted_practices: Involve impacted stakeholders and subject matter experts (e.g., in bias or ethics) in overseeing end-to-end AI development and deliberating on use cases.
Apply one or more validated implementation, evaluation, and long-term use frameworks (e.g., UTAUT) to ensure adoption barriers are measurably considered.

Develop assessment toolkits with critical questions or criteria for each adoption domain (bias, ethics, explainability) and use them to gather evidence and apply adjustments where criteria are not met.
Incorporate cognitive-socio-technical considerations, including impacts on patients, clinicians, and workflows, into AI governance frameworks.
Provide governance oversight of bias, equity, transparency, ethics, explainability, data handling, and safety with gated mechanisms across the AI lifecycle.

screen.reason: This paper presents a framework and commentary proposing an AI governance structure for healthcare organizations to safely implement and adopt AI systems.
